metric-n_submissions-desc: Number of landings recorded by enumerators and kept after validation.
metric-n_fishers-desc: Average number of fishers on a surveyed trip (the crew size).
metric-trip_duration_hrs-desc: Average length of a surveyed trip, in hours, as reported at landing.
metric-mean_cpue-desc: Kilograms of catch per fisher per hour of the trip: how hard it is to catch fish.
metric-mean_rpue-desc: Value of the catch per fisher per hour of the trip, in {{currency}}.
metric-mean_price_kg-desc: Average price of a kilogram of catch at the landing site.
info-grid-resolution-value: squares {{size}} wide at this zoom (from 500 m to 50 km as you zoom out).
info-each-cell: Each gathers the fishing cells inside it, hexagons of about 0.1 km² where tracked boats fished on at least 3 trips: its colour is the band of its busiest cell, its height the average fishing hours per day of its cells.
info-time-ranges: Fishing hours per day (select to filter)
info-avg-time: {{value}}h of fishing per active day, on average
info-max-time: {{value}}h of fishing per active day, at most
info-grounds-definition: outlined areas of neighbouring cells fished regularly. Hover over one to see its figures.
info-visits-definition: A visit is one trip fishing in one cell, so a trip that crosses several cells counts in each.
info-rotate-hint: Shift + drag, or drag with the right button, to tilt and rotate.
metric-estimated_revenue-desc: Estimated total value of the catch landed by all the boats of the district, added up over the months shown.
metric-estimated_catch_tn-desc: Estimated total catch landed by all the boats of the district, added up over the months shown.
text-no-data-available-for-filters: No data available for selected filters
text-district-species-description: Recorded catch (kg) of the 15 most-landed species groups, by district
text-no-length-data-available: No length data available for selected districts
text-no-data-available-for-districts: No data available for selected districts
text-select-districts: Select at least one district to see this chart.
text-page-error-description: This page hit an unexpected error. Reload to try again.
text-page-not-found-description: The page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved.
metric-mean_cpue-how: For each surveyed landing, the catch is divided by the number of fishers and the hours the trip lasted. Landings are averaged by district and month; districts and months are then combined, weighted by their number of landings.
metric-mean_cpue-limits: A falling rate can mean fewer fish, but also bad weather or a change of gear or fishing ground. A steady rate can hide a declining stock when fishers work harder or move. Read it as a warning sign, not a measure of the stock.
metric-mean_rpue-how: For each surveyed landing, the value of the catch is divided by the number of fishers and the hours the trip lasted, then averaged in the same way as catch per unit effort.
metric-mean_rpue-limits: The value is what fishers report at the landing site. It is not adjusted for inflation.
metric-mean_catch_kg-desc: Average catch landed by one fishing trip.
metric-mean_catch_kg-how: The mean total catch of the surveyed landings, by district and month, then combined weighted by landings.
metric-mean_catch_kg-limits: Depends on which boats and gears are surveyed: a district where larger boats are surveyed more often shows a larger catch per trip.
metric-mean_catch_price-desc: Average value of the catch landed by one fishing trip.
metric-mean_catch_price-how: The mean value of the surveyed landings, by district and month, then combined weighted by landings.
metric-mean_catch_price-limits: Covers the whole crew's catch, not one person's income, and does not subtract fuel, gear or other costs.
metric-n_fishers-how: The mean crew size of the surveyed landings, by district and month.
metric-n_fishers-limits: This is the crew size, not the number of fishers in a district.
metric-n_submissions-how: A count of the validated landing records, by district and month. Totals add up across months and districts.
metric-n_submissions-limits: Enumerators do not record every landing, so this counts the sample, not all fishing trips. Figures resting on fewer than 10 landings carry a warning sign.
metric-trip_duration_hrs-how: The mean trip duration reported for the surveyed landings, by district and month.
metric-trip_duration_hrs-limits: The duration is what fishers report when they land, not a measured time.
metric-mean_price_kg-how: For each landing, the value of the catch divided by its weight, averaged by district and month.
metric-mean_price_kg-limits: All species are mixed together, so a change in what is landed moves the price as much as a change in the market.
metric-estimated_fishing_trips-desc: Estimated number of fishing trips made by all the boats of the district, added up over the months shown.
metric-estimated_fishing_trips-how: Boats in the district × the trips a boat makes in the month, measured on the boats that carry a GPS tracker.
metric-estimated_fishing_trips-limits: Assumes tracked boats fish as often as the rest of the fleet.
metric-estimated_catch_tn-how: Boats in the district × trips per tracked boat × catch of a surveyed trip, month by month.
metric-estimated_catch_tn-limits: An estimate built on two samples, surveyed landings and tracked boats. It leaves out fishing without boats, such as gleaning on foot. Trust the order of magnitude and the trend more than the exact figure.
metric-estimated_revenue-how: Boats in the district × trips per tracked boat × value of a surveyed trip, month by month.
metric-estimated_revenue-limits: Same limits as the estimated catch. Values are those reported at landing, not market or export prices.
metric-estimated_fishing_trips_fao-desc: Estimated number of fishing trips made by all the boats of the district, added up over the months shown.
metric-estimated_fishing_trips_fao-how: For each gear or boat type: boats in the census × days a boat fishes in the month, as surveyed fishers report them, one trip per day fished.
metric-estimated_fishing_trips_fao-limit: Rests on fishers' memory of the days they fished. Counted only where the catch is estimated: a district and month with fewer than 10 surveyed trips has none.
metric-estimated_catch_tn_fao-desc: Estimated total catch landed by all the boats of the district, added up over the months shown.
metric-estimated_catch_tn_fao-how: For each gear or boat type: boats in the census × days a boat fishes in the month, as surveyed fishers report them × catch of a surveyed trip; then added up. FAO's standard method, from its OPEN ARTFISH toolkit.
metric-estimated_catch_tn_fao-limits: Counts only the gears or boat types surveyed that month. A district and month with fewer than 10 surveyed trips has no estimate. It leaves out fishing without boats, such as gleaning on foot.
metric-estimated_revenue_fao-desc: Estimated total value of the catch landed by all the boats of the district, added up over the months shown.
metric-estimated_revenue_fao-how: For each gear or boat type: boats in the census × days a boat fishes in the month, as surveyed fishers report them × value of a surveyed trip; then added up.
metric-estimated_revenue_fao-limits: Same limits as the estimated catch. Values are those reported at landing, not market or export prices.
text-confidence-tracked: {{pct}}% of the district's boats carried a GPS tracker
info-district-table-what: Each district over the selected months: ranked by one measure, on the map, or with every measure in one table.
info-district-table-how: Totals are added up over the months, averages weighted by the landings behind each month. Tracker confidence is the share of the district's boats with a GPS tracker: high from 30%, medium from 10%, low below.
info-district-table-limits: Districts with few landings can show extreme values. Compare districts on rates or catch per trip rather than on totals, which grow with the size of the fleet.
info-methods-limits: The two methods use different data, so their figures differ: trackers record how often tracked boats fish, ARTFISH uses the days fishers say they fished. Totals add up only the district-months both estimate. Neither covers fishing without boats.
info-map-what: Where boats with GPS trackers fish: columns whose colour and height give the hours of fishing per active day, with the fishing grounds they keep returning to outlined.
info-map-how: A model reads each GPS track and keeps only the time spent fishing, not travelling. The map adds up every tracked trip since tracking began, whatever months are selected, and leaves out cells with fewer than 3 trips. Hours are summed over boats, so two boats fishing the same hour count two.
info-map-limits: Only boats that carry a tracker appear on the map, so areas fished by untracked boats look empty. Fishing time is predicted from the tracks, not recorded.
text-seasonality-description: Average for each calendar month over every year of data
info-seasonality-what: Which months tend to be high or low in each district.
info-seasonality-how: The value of each calendar month is averaged over the years with data. The time range picked above does not apply here.
info-seasonality-limits: Needs at least two years of data. With only two or three years, one unusual year can still shape the pattern.
info-gear-landings-what: For each gear: its share of the surveyed landings, its catch and revenue per fisher per hour, the share of its catch below maturity, and its main species.
info-gear-landings-how: Shares are of the landings surveyed in the selected districts and months. The share below maturity is a range, from species with a known length at maturity, and needs at least 10 landings with measured fish.
info-gear-landings-limits: Describes the surveyed landings, not the whole fleet. Enumerators may visit some landing sites, and so some gears, more often than others.
info-maturity-what: For each species with a known length at maturity, how much of its measured catch was landed before the fish could reproduce.
info-maturity-how: A length class wholly below the FishBase length at maturity counts as caught small; one that contains it could hold fish on either side. So each bar is a range, its figures beside it: the solid part is the least share, the lighter part the most.
info-maturity-limits: Only single species measured on at least 10 landings are listed, and shares are by weight. Wide length classes make wide ranges, and FishBase lengths at maturity may come from other regions.
text-length-frequency-description: Share of the measured catch per cm of length
info-lengths-what: How the recorded catch of one species splits across length classes, and how much of it was smaller than the length at which the species first reproduces.
info-lengths-how: Each class shows its share of the species' measured catch over the selected districts and months. The bands below maturity, at optimum length and of large spawners use FishBase lengths; a class across a band's edge counts only towards the upper end of the range.
info-lengths-limits: Shares are by weight, so large fish count for more than they would by number. Groups of several species have no single length at maturity. Only species measured on at least 10 landings are listed.
text-no-maturity-for-species: No length at maturity is known for this species or group, so its catch can't be compared with one.
info-composition-what: Which species groups make up the catch recorded at the surveyed landings.
info-composition-how: The catch weight of each species group at the surveyed landings, added up over the selected districts and months.
info-composition-limits: This is the catch of the surveyed landings only, a small part of the total. Some groups are recorded at family or genus level.
text-trophic-level-description: Average position of the recorded catch in the food web, month by month
info-trophic-what: Whether the catch is shifting between predators (high trophic level) and plant or plankton eaters (low).
info-trophic-how: Each species group takes the median FishBase trophic level of its species. The monthly value is their average, weighted by recorded catch.
info-trophic-limits: A slow fall over years can signal that large predators are being fished out. From month to month it moves with seasons, markets and what enumerators identify, so read long trends only.
text-species-price-description: {{currency}} per kg at the landing site
info-species-price-what: The price fishers get for a kilogram of each of the most-landed species.
info-species-price-limits: Species that are mostly landed together with others can be missing or rest on few trips.
text-no-species-price: No species prices in the selected districts and months.
text-vulnerability-bands-description: Share of the recorded catch, month by month
info-vulnerability-what: How much of the catch comes from species that recover slowly from fishing: large, long-lived species that reproduce late.
info-vulnerability-how: FishBase scores each species' intrinsic vulnerability to fishing from 0 to 100, from its life history, such as its maximum size, growth and age at maturity. A species group takes the median of its species and is placed in one of four equal bands.
info-vulnerability-limits: The score describes the species, not the state of the local stock. For groups of many species the median can hide very vulnerable members; the table below shows the range.
text-sharks-rays-description: Share of the recorded catch, month by month
info-sharks-what: How much of the recorded catch is sharks and rays, which grow slowly and have few young.
info-sharks-how: Species groups that FishBase classes as sharks and rays (Elasmobranchii), as a share of each month's recorded catch.
info-sharks-limits: Only counts the sharks and rays that enumerators recorded.
text-no-sharks-rays: No sharks or rays were recorded in the selected districts and months.
info-status-what: For each species group: its share of the recorded catch, its vulnerability to fishing, its IUCN Red List status, its CITES listing and its trophic level.
info-status-how: From FishBase and SeaLifeBase. For a single species the IUCN category is shown. For a group, the table shows how many of its species are threatened (Vulnerable, Endangered or Critically Endangered) and the range of their vulnerability scores.
info-status-limits: IUCN categories are global and can be years old. National protection rules are not included yet.
text-coverage-description: Landings surveyed per district and month, last {{count}} months
methods-estimates-body: Recorded figures describe the landings that enumerators surveyed. Estimated figures scale them up to all the boats of a district, month by month. The dashboard makes them by two methods and shows both side by side.
methods-confidence-body: This method assumes that tracked boats fish as often as the rest of the fleet. The larger the share of boats tracked, the safer that assumption, so the share sets the confidence of its estimates. While fewer than 10% of a district's boats are tracked, the dashboard does not show their change on a year earlier.
methods-species-body: Each species group recorded at landing is matched to its species in FishBase and SeaLifeBase, among those recorded in the Western and Eastern Indian Ocean (FAO areas 51 and 57). From there come the vulnerability to fishing, the trophic level, the IUCN Red List category, the CITES listing and the lengths at maturity and at optimum. A group of several species takes the median vulnerability and trophic level of its species and counts how many of them are threatened (IUCN Vulnerable, Endangered or Critically Endangered).
methods-sizes-body: Lengths are grouped in classes: under 10 cm, then 5 cm wide up to 30 cm, 10 cm wide up to 1 m, and wider above. Following Froese (2004), the size views show the share of the catch below the length at maturity, within 10% of the optimum length (where a year-class reaches its greatest total weight) and above it, as large spawners. A length class that holds the length at maturity has fish on both sides of it, so the share below maturity is a range, as the diagram shows. Sizes are shown for species groups measured on at least 10 landings, and compared with the lengths at maturity and optimum only for those identified to a single species.
methods-glossary-landing: A boat's return to shore with its catch: the unit the surveys record.
methods-glossary-district: An administrative area (GAUL level 2), the finest level these figures are broken down by.
methods-glossary-trip: One outing of a boat and its crew, from departure to landing.
methods-glossary-cpue: Catch per unit effort: kilograms of catch per fisher per hour of the trip.
methods-glossary-rpue: Revenue per unit effort: value of the catch per fisher per hour of the trip.
methods-glossary-recorded: Measured on the surveyed landings themselves.
methods-glossary-estimated: Scaled up from the surveyed landings to all the boats of a district, by the GPS tracker method or the FAO ARTFISH method.
methods-glossary-tracker-method: Raises the surveyed catch to the fleet from how often GPS-tracked boats fish: boats listed × trips per tracked boat × catch per surveyed trip.
methods-glossary-artfish-method: FAO's standard way of raising a landing survey to the fleet: boats in the census × days fished, as fishers report them × catch per surveyed trip, by gear or boat type.
methods-glossary-taxon: What enumerators record a catch as: a species, or a genus or family when the fish are hard to tell apart.
methods-glossary-length-class: The size band a fish is recorded in, for example 20–25 cm.
methods-glossary-maturity: The length at which fish of a species first reproduce, from FishBase.
methods-glossary-trophic: Place in the food web: about 2 for plant eaters, 3 to 4.5 for predators.
methods-glossary-vulnerability: A FishBase score from 0 to 100 of how vulnerable a species is to fishing, from its life history: large, slow-growing species that mature late score high.
methods-contact-questions: About these figures, the dashboard or access to the data.
methods-contact-platform: For survey teams: review flagged records and download the data, with an account from the Peskas team.
methods-contact-api: The landing records for your own analysis in R, Python or a spreadsheet, with a key from the Peskas team.
methods-contact-peskas: WorldFish's open-source platform for monitoring small-scale fisheries.
text-too-few-months: This chart needs at least two months of data.
text-traits-not-published: Species information (FishBase traits) isn't published for this dashboard yet. It arrives with the next data update.
text-lengths-not-published: Fish sizes aren't published for this dashboard yet. They arrive with the next data update.
text-spanning-maturity-short: Possibly below: its size class spans maturity size
title-seasonality: {{metric}}: in which months is it higher or lower?
title-length-frequency: At what size are fish caught?
title-district-species: Which species does each district land most?
title-trophic-level: Is the catch moving down the food web?
title-species-price: What is each species worth at landing?
title-vulnerability-bands: Are slow-recovering species a growing part of the catch?
title-sharks-rays: How much of the catch is sharks and rays?
title-species-status: How threatened are the species landed?
info-coverage-what: How many landings enumerators surveyed in each district and month.
info-coverage-how: A count of the validated landing records, month by month, over the last two years.
info-coverage-limits: Blank cells are months with no survey, not months with no fishing.
text-gear-species-not-published: Catch by gear and species isn't published for this dashboard yet. It arrives with the next data update.
text-too-few-measured-species: No species has at least {{min}} landings with measured fish in this selection.
info-composition-limits-sample: This survey identifies a sample of each catch, so these weights are of that sample.
info-species-price-how-species: Each species in a catch has its own price. Prices are averaged over districts and months, weighted by catch.
info-species-price-how-trip: Fishers report one value for the whole catch, so a species gets a price only from trips that landed that species alone. Prices are averaged over districts and months, weighted by catch.
methods-prices-body-species: Reported at the landing site as a price per kilogram for each species in the sample.
methods-prices-body-trip: Reported at the landing site as one value for the whole catch, so a species price comes only from landings of that species alone.
methods-sizes-body-means: This survey records, for each species on a landing, the average length of the fish measured, so the classes hold those averages: their spread is narrower than that of the fish, and the smallest and largest fish are understated.
methods-glossary-optimum: The length at which a year-class of a species reaches its greatest total weight, from its growth in FishBase.
text-lengths-means-note: Each length here is the average of the fish measured on one landing, so the chart shows how those averages spread; single fish vary more, so the smallest and largest fish are understated.

text-species-ranking-footer: These {{count}} groups are {{share}} of the recorded catch, out of {{total}} groups.
text-length-axis: Length (cm); each bar is as wide as its length class
text-caught-small-description: Share of the measured catch below the length at maturity, for species measured on {{min}} or more landings. Select one to see its sizes.
text-gear-profile-description: One row per gear, in order of use. Faded rows rest on fewer than 10 landings.
text-gear-species-description: Share of each gear's recorded catch by species group ({{species}} largest groups, {{gears}} most-used gears)
text-selection-average-weighted: Average of the selected districts, weighted by landings
text-multiples-axis: Every panel shares one axis, from 0 to {{max}}.
text-vulnerability-score: Score (for a group, the median of its species)

text-estimates-no-change: Change on a year earlier not shown
methods-flow-label: From the data collected to the figures on this dashboard
methods-flow-surveys-detail: Enumerators record landings at landing sites on KoboToolbox.
methods-flow-checked-detail: Records flagged as likely errors are left out.
methods-flow-recorded-detail: Catch, value, crew and hours of the surveyed landings, and the species and sizes caught.
methods-flow-per-trip: Catch, value and days fished per surveyed trip
methods-flow-trackers-detail: Some boats carry a tracker that records each trip.
methods-flow-trips-detail: By district and month, each boat in the district where most of its trips land.
methods-flow-boats-detail: The number of boats listed for each district, by gear or boat type.
methods-flow-tracked-detail: Tracked boats divided by all boats: the confidence of the estimates.
methods-flow-estimated-detail: Trips, catch and revenue of all the boats of a district, by the GPS tracker and FAO ARTFISH methods.
methods-flow-fishbase-detail: Species recorded in the Western and Eastern Indian Ocean (FAO areas 51 and 57).
methods-flow-traits-detail: Matched to each species group recorded at landing.
methods-flow-species-detail: Vulnerability, IUCN category, trophic level, and lengths at maturity and at optimum.
text-partner-TZ: Developed by WorldFish in collaboration with the Zanzibar Fisheries and Marine Resources Research Institute (ZAFIRI).
text-partner-KE: Developed by WorldFish in collaboration with the Kenya Fisheries Service (KEFS).
text-partner-MZ: Developed by WorldFish in collaboration with Mozambique's National Directorate of Fisheries and Aquaculture (DINAPA).
methods-fact-survey-TZ: Enumerators from the Zanzibar Fisheries and Marine Resources Research Institute (ZAFIRI) record landings at landing sites in Unguja and Pemba.
methods-fact-survey-KE: The catch assessment survey of the Kenya Fisheries Service (KEFS), recorded on KEFS's own KoboToolbox server.
methods-fact-survey-MZ: The landing survey of DINAPA, Mozambique's National Directorate of Fisheries and Aquaculture.
methods-fact-recorded-TZ: Gear, number of fishers, how long the trip lasted, the catch of each species group (number and length of the fish, or number of buckets) and the value of the whole catch.
methods-fact-recorded-MZ: Gear, number of fishers, how long the trip lasted, the catch of each species group (number and length of the fish, or number of buckets) and the value of the whole catch.
methods-fact-recorded-KE: Gear, number of fishers, the start and end time of the trip, the weight and value of the whole catch, and a sample of it identified to species, weighed and priced per kilogram. Fish of some species are measured.
methods-fact-weight-TZ: Worked out from the number and length of the fish with FishBase and SeaLifeBase length-weight formulas; when no length is recorded, from the number of buckets and the weight of a bucket.
methods-fact-weight-MZ: Worked out from the number and length of the fish with FishBase and SeaLifeBase length-weight formulas; when no length is recorded, from the number of buckets and the weight of a bucket.
methods-fact-weight-KE: Recorded for the whole catch at landing. The share of each species comes from the sample.
methods-fact-trackers: Some boats carry a solar-powered GPS tracker from Pelagic Data Systems, which records where each trip goes and how long it lasts.
methods-fact-checks: Each record is checked for likely errors, such as an impossible crew size or trip duration, or a catch, fish length or price far outside the usual range. Flagged records are left out of these figures; survey teams review them in the Peskas Management Platform.
methods-formula-trips-per-boat: Trips per tracked boat in the month
methods-formula-per-trip: Catch or value per surveyed trip
methods-confidence-scale: Confidence of the estimates, by the share of the district's boats tracked
methods-artfish-body: The FAO ARTFISH method is FAO's standard way of raising a landing survey to the whole fleet, as its OPEN ARTFISH toolkit sets out. It needs no trackers. For each gear or boat type, it multiplies the boats in the census by the days a boat fishes in the month, from what surveyed fishers say they fished the week before, and by the catch or value of a surveyed trip; then it adds them up. A district gets an estimate for a month when it has at least 10 surveyed trips, so this method also covers districts and months without tracked boats.
methods-artfish-days-KE: In Kenya the question on days fished is part of the KEFS survey, whose trips are the ones this method uses.
methods-artfish-days-TZ: In Zanzibar the question on days fished has been asked since August 2025; earlier months use the district's average answer over all months.
methods-artfish-days-MZ: In Mozambique the question on days fished is part of the DINAPA survey, whose trips are the ones this method uses.
methods-artfish-precision: FAO's method can also tell how precise each estimate is. This dashboard doesn't show that yet, so it doesn't show the change of an ARTFISH figure on a year earlier.
methods-artfish-reference-link: de Graaf, Stamatopoulos & Jarrett (2017), OPEN ARTFISH and the FAO ODK mobile phone application: a toolkit for small-scale fisheries routine data collection, FAO
methods-compare-differ: The two methods rest on different data, so their figures differ. The GPS tracker method counts the trips that trackers record; ARTFISH counts the days fishers say they fished. Both weight the catch by the mix of boats and gears in the census. ARTFISH also estimates districts and months without tracked boats, which the GPS tracker method cannot.
methods-compare-totals: The totals and trend lines add up only the district-months both methods estimate, so they compare like with like; where one method has no estimate for the districts and months selected, the other shows alone. The district panels draw every month each method estimates, and each district's own figures follow the same rule over its months.

methods-tracker-summary: How often boats fish, from the boats that carry a GPS tracker.
methods-artfish-summary: FAO's standard method: how often boats fish, from what fishers say.
methods-tracker-body: A district gets an estimate for a month only when it has both tracked trips and surveyed landings that month.
text-estimates-two: By the GPS tracker method and FAO's ARTFISH method, over the districts and months both estimate.
text-estimates-rounded-both: Estimates are rounded. Their change on a year earlier isn't shown: never for ARTFISH, and not for the GPS tracker method while fewer than 10% of boats are tracked.
methods-artfish-formula-label: How the FAO ARTFISH estimates are calculated
methods-artfish-formula-boats: Boats in the census, by gear or boat type
methods-artfish-formula-days: Days a boat fishes in the month, as fishers report them
methods-artfish-formula-per-trip: Catch or value per surveyed trip
methods-artfish-formula-totals: Estimated catch or revenue, added up over gears or boat types
methods-size-caption: Illustration, not data: a species that matures at 45 cm, with an optimum length of 55 cm. Lengths in cm.
methods-key-few: Fewer than 10 surveyed landings behind a figure. It can swing widely from one month to the next.
methods-key-faded: A bar or table row resting on fewer than 10 landings is drawn faded.
methods-key-hollow: In the district panels, a month with fewer than 10 landings.
methods-key-change: The change on the same months a year earlier.
methods-key-approx: An estimate, by either method, rounded to two significant figures.
methods-key-grey: The grey line: the same months a year earlier in the trend chart of a recorded figure, the average of the selected districts in the district panels.
methods-key-methods: A wine-red line and a gold one: the same estimate by the GPS tracker method (wine-red) and the FAO ARTFISH method (gold).
methods-key-range: A share known only between two bounds: at least the solid part, at most the end of the lighter part.
methods-reading-combined: Every figure covers complete months: the current month is left out until its data is in, and a change compares the same months a year earlier. Averages over districts, months or gears are weighted by the landings behind each value, so a district with 500 landings counts for more than one with 5.
methods-reading-limits: Catch by species is the catch recorded at the surveyed landings: it shows what the catch is made of, not how much was landed in total. The fishing-effort map shows only boats that carry a GPS tracker, over all the time they have been tracked. None of these figures is a stock assessment: catch rates, sizes and vulnerability show where to look more closely.
methods-reading-sample: The survey records the weight of the whole catch and identifies and measures a sample of it, so catch by species describes that sample.
section-recorded-all-time: measured on {{landings}} landings over every month of data; pick 3, 6 or 12 months to compare with a year earlier
text-unlisted-districts_one: Landings were also recorded in {{districts}}, a district this dashboard doesn't list yet; they are left out of every figure.
text-unlisted-districts_other: Landings were also recorded in {{districts}}, districts this dashboard doesn't list yet; they are left out of every figure.
text-load-error: Reload the page to try again. If it keeps failing, the data service may be down.
text-map-no-effort: No tracked fishing to show yet.
text-map-no-districts: No district has a value for these months.
text-map-unsupported: This browser can't draw the map: it needs WebGL.
text-multiples-point: point at a month to read it in every district
